title: public.ficia_time_entries is referenced by a migration but created by none

what.statement: COMMENT ON TABLE public.ficia_time_entries IS 'FICIA timesheet & attendance entries.';
what.consequence: The 32-migration set cannot rebuild the database from scratch. Every migration after this point is unreachable on a clean database, which is why the local PostgreSQL twin stops here.

whyNotFixedHere: No tracked migration creates the table, so the authoritative definition is not in this repository.
The only description of its shape is src/integrations/supabase/types.ts, which is GENERATED OUTPUT and was explicitly excluded as a source.
types.ts describes column names and nullability only. It does not carry RLS policies, GRANTs, defaults, CHECK constraints, ON DELETE behaviour, or index definitions.

Writing a CREATE TABLE from those types would produce a table with no row-level security on timesheet and attendance data. That converts a build failure, which is loud and harmless, into a cross-tenant data-exposure bug, which is silent and not. A migration set that rebuilds but leaks is worse than one that refuses to rebuild.

types.ts additionally records foreign keys ficia_time_entries_correction_of_fkey (self-referential) and ficia_time_entries_department_id_fkey. Their ON DELETE and ON UPDATE actions are not recoverable from generated types, and guessing them would silently change deletion semantics for payroll-relevant records.

credentialsChecked.supabaseCli: available (2.110.0) but cannot link or dump without an access token and database password
credentialsChecked.conclusion: The publishable/anon key cannot read pg_catalog, pg_policies or information_schema for a definition dump. No authoritative schema is reachable from this environment.

exactResolution.owner: whoever owns the Supabase project that already contains this table
exactResolution.step1: Authenticate the CLI: supabase login (or set SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN)
exactResolution.step3: supabase db dump --schema public --table ficia_time_entries > authoritative.sql
exactResolution.step4: Also dump the policies: supabase db dump --data-only=false --schema public | grep -A20 ficia_time_entries, or query pg_policies for policies on the table
exactResolution.step5: Add the recovered definition as a migration ordered BEFORE 20260721153321, with its own verification and rollback files, matching supabase/APPLY_ORDER.md
exactResolution.step6: Re-run the local twin to confirm the set rebuilds from scratch, then re-run cross-tenant attack tests

acceptanceForClosure: A CREATE TABLE migration for public.ficia_time_entries exists and is ordered before 20260721153321
Its RLS policies, GRANTs, indexes and foreign-key actions come from the live project, not from generated types
The full migration set applies cleanly to an empty database
Cross-tenant attack tests pass against the created table
